escalation_reason: STABILIZED, NOT RESOLVED. mark_dlq_permanent executed successfully and list_dlq_messages confirmed it landed on eb798430-c3ad-5a44-b7d7-d15ab54d3f76 — this is an escalation by design, not a failed remediation. mark_dlq_permanent is a stabilize-only action: fences one dead-lettered job out of auto-replay — it sets `remediation_hint=human_required` and writes the operator's reason to the audit trail, and the platform's own description says it "doesn't change job.status — the entry stays in DLQ". So the job is still dead and its work is still undone: the fence stops a later bulk replay from re-running a poisoned payload, and it fixes nothing about why the payload failed. The bad data, the producer bug or the schema behind it is untouched and a human still has to act. Unlike a pause the fence does not expire, so nothing is on a clock — but 'permanent' describes the fence, not the incident. The underlying fault on eb798430-c3ad-5a44-b7d7-d15ab54d3f76 is unchanged and still needs a human decision on the real fix. Treat the stabilization as a clock, not an outcome.

findings: One dead-letter row was carrying no classification at all: job eb798430-c3ad-5a44-b7d7-d15ab54d3f76 (bulk_api_sync), remediation_hint=null, dead after three attempts on "SchemaValidationError: payload missing required field 'job_id' (received keys: [])" — the message that was published carried no fields at all, so validation rejects it identically every time. This is a fault in the SENDER, not in the platform and not in the data of any file: no replay can add a field the message does not contain. Because nothing had categorised it, a bulk or category replay could still have swept it up. It is now fenced with mark_dlq_permanent: classified human_required, stamped with fenced_at, excluded from any future auto-replay, still dead-lettered, work still undone. The other four rows in the queue (one replay_safe, two wait_and_replay, one already human_required) were left untouched — they are not this incident.
recommendation: Fix the producer, then re-submit: whatever published to job.submitted sent an empty payload, so the required field 'job_id' was never there to read. The fence stops auto-replay and nothing else, so the job stays dead until the sender emits a valid message — do not replay it from the DLQ, it will fail identically. Two follow-ups worth having: schema validation at the producer so an invalid message is rejected where it is written rather than three attempts later, and triage coverage for rows like this one, which reached the dead-letter queue with no category on it at all.
